thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Markets Mixed, Retreating Then Recovering As Tech And Energy Stocks Lead

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Markets Mixed, Retreating Then Recovering As Tech And Energy Stocks Lead
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Nikkei nears 1-month low
Asian stock markets mostly fell early but improved from the worst levels of the day, including a flip to positive territory in Hong Kong, as the region's trading tracked the drubbing Tuesday for U.S. stocks and oil futures. Both equities and oil markets indicated a Wednesday rebound was in order.
Japan's Nikkei was down 0.4%, moving close to its lowest point in a month as energy and electronics stocks slid. Oil explorer Inpex (1605.TO) was down 3.2% while Sumitomo (8053.TO) , which has various natural-resource investments around the world, lost 3.2%. Meanwhile, Olympus (7733.TO) dropped 8.7% and Mitsubishi Electric (6503.TO) was off 2.7%. Nissan shares (NSANY) reversed a bit of yesterday's slide following the arrest of CEO Carlos Ghosn (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/renault-appoints-interim-ceo-chairman-after-ghosns-arrest-2018-11-20).
Hong Kong stocks extended losses initially though the Hang Seng Index closed up 0.5% after dropping more than 1% early on. While tech stocks lagged overall, Tencent (0700.HK) gained 2.8% and AAC (2018.HK) rose 1.9%. Oil company Cnooc (0883.HK) fell 2.5%.
In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite were both up slightly after early weakness. Energy stocks lagged after the latest plunge in oil prices Tuesday.
Sagging energy stocks also weighed down Australia's ASX 200 , with Woodside Petroleum (WPL.AU) down 2% and Santos (STO.AU) off 4.3%. New Zealand's benchmark was down slightly.
South Korea's Kospi declined 0.3%, as Samsung (005930.SE) dipped. Singapore's Strai Times Index rose 0.4% while Taiwan's Taiex slipped 0.03% as Apple (AAPL) suppliers Foxconn (2354.TW) and Largan Precision (3008.TW) fell.
